newsitem.title: USA: McVeigh prints found on documents - report.
newsitem.headline: McVeigh prints found on documents - report.

text.p: The fingerprints and handwriting of accused bomber Timothy McVeigh have been found on documents linked to a phone card the government says was used to buy bomb materials to destroy the Oklahoma City federal building, CBS News reported on Wednesday night.

While experts have testified that McVeigh's prints were not on the card itself, CBS quoted sources as saying that prosecutors found the 29-year-old Gulf War veteran's prints and handwriting on documents including an application for the card and money orders to make payments for it.
After the network's broadcast, a prosecution source told reporters that the items had not been entered into evidence yet but would be made public soon.

The card was issued to a "Daryl Bridges" and was found at the home of McVeigh's alleged co-conspirator, Terry Nichols. Only Nichols' prints were found on the card itself, according to court testimony. Nichols is to be tried separately. Both men have pleaded not guilty.

The prosecution has spent the better part of two days laying the foundation to have the calls made on the card entered into evidence. Government lawyers said the calls match McVeigh's travels through the country and were made to companies that sell explosives, detonator cords and fertiliser.
Also included in the calls made on the card were two to a Ryder truck office in Kansas where the truck used to ferry the bomb that destroyed the Alfred P. Murrah building was rented.
The defence had objected to the calls being entered into evidence on the grounds that the prosecution cannot prove who made the calls or why they were made.
